_comment: Accepted pnpm-audit exceptions — task-prod-runtime-vulns (2026-08-16/17, round 3 per security-review PR #536); round 4 (2026-09-02, infra/audit-undici-advisories) added the @xmldom/xmldom group below. Read scripts/devops/check-pnpm-audit.mjs's module doc before editing. Every group below is keyed by exact GHSA id (not just a package name) — a NEW advisory id for an already-listed package is NOT covered and will gate CI red until it is triaged and either fixed or added here with its own reason. Every group MUST carry a `reason` of meaningful length (enforced by the guard, not just convention) — an empty or placeholder reason makes the guard treat the whole group as unaccepted regardless of severity. Round 2: vite/postcss/nanoid/@babel/core/js-yaml/qs/brace-expansion were ALL genuinely fixed (not just documented) after security-review found the earlier 'no fix below a major' reasons factually wrong for several of them — dependency bump + `pnpm dedupe`, or a root pnpm.overrides entry, none crossing a version-pins.md pin. Round 3: `esbuild` (round 2's remaining exception) is ALSO genuinely fixed now — a naive blanket `esbuild` override broke `pnpm build` (Vite's OWN internal esbuild@0.25.12 dependency, itself never vulnerable to either GHSA, conflicts with a forced newer version underneath it), but a SELECTOR override scoped to only the two actually-vulnerable consumers (`"tsx>esbuild"`, `"@esbuild-kit/core-utils>esbuild"` in root package.json) resolves both without ever touching Vite's own untouched, unaffected esbuild edge. Round 4: the gate went red again on `main` from FOUR newly-published advisories against packages that already had a pnpm.overrides floor from earlier rounds (qs >=6.15.2, fastify ^5.12.0, fast-uri >=3.1.5) — the floor itself hadn't moved since it was set, but newer CVEs raised the bar above it. All three were genuinely fixed by tightening the existing override floor (qs >=6.16.0, fastify ^5.12.1, fast-uri >=3.1.6 — still inside the ^5.8.5 fastify pin, no pin crossed); a fourth advisory (@xmldom/xmldom) was deliberately NOT fixed the same way at that time (historical; that group no longer exists — see Round 6 at the end). `pnpm --filter @crm/web build` before/after: identical PWA precache (99 entries, 3700.99 KiB) — none of the touched packages reach the shipped SPA bundle. Round 5 (2026-10-02, infra/audit-gate-refresh): gate red again on 28 newly-published advisories. 22 genuinely fixed by version bumps (axios ^1.20.0, @nestjs/platform-fastify ^11.2.4, overrides fastify ^5.12.5 / fast-uri >=3.1.8 / brace-expansion >=5.0.12 — no version-pins.md pin crossed; Fastify stays inside ^5.8.5 line); 6 new undici advisories added to the existing dev-only undici group (jsdom test polyfill, same reachability proof as before). Round 6 (2026-10-22, devops/vitest-audit-advisories): vitest 4.1.11 -> 4.1.12 genuinely fixed GHSA-qxg6-89mg-rqv8 and GHSA-xp26-3454-mjgp (@vitest/mocker); no exception added. The @xmldom/xmldom group (10 GHSA ids) was REMOVED, not carried over: the lockfile resolves @xmldom/xmldom 0.8.15 (patched) via the single apps/api -> mammoth edge (pnpm why @xmldom/xmldom -r) and pnpm audit reports none of those ids. The removed group justified itself with a claim that bumping to 0.8.15 would break resume-text-extraction.service.spec.ts; that claim was STALE — the spec was already rebuilt for 0.8.15 and passes (checked 2026-10-22). A stale justification keeps a dead exception alive, so re-verify any reason before copying it forward.

exceptions.reason: `braces` (3.0.3, the LATEST published release; the advisory's patched range is `<0.0.0`, i.e. NO fixed version exists on npm, so an override/bump is impossible) is reachable only through devDependency chains: `pnpm why braces -r` shows every path under `devDependencies:` — root lint-staged -> micromatch -> braces, root eslint-plugin-lingui -> micromatch -> braces, root and apps/web @lingui/cli (and @lingui/vite-plugin -> @lingui/cli) -> chokidar / micromatch -> braces. Zero paths under `dependencies:` in apps/api, apps/web or packages/shared: these are glob-matching helpers of the pre-commit hook, ESLint and the Lingui message-extraction CLI, never bundled into the shipped SPA nor loaded by the API runtime. GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm is a stack-exhaustion DoS triggered by deeply nested brace patterns passed to braces(); the patterns fed to these tools come from our own committed config/globs and file names in the repository, not from untrusted input, and the worst outcome is a crashed local/CI dev command. Fix path: re-check when braces publishes a patched release (then add an override floor), or when micromatch/chokidar drop it. Round 6 (2026-10-03, infra/audit-gate-refresh-2026-10-03): the same run also reported two @fastify/busboy advisories (GHSA-xjh9-v7x6-24jw, GHSA-x8mw-p69m-v3mx); those ARE production-reachable (apps/api -> @fastify/multipart -> @fastify/busboy, file uploads) and were genuinely fixed by a `@fastify/busboy >=3.2.1 <4.0.0` pnpm.overrides floor (resolves 3.2.2; @fastify/multipart declares ^3.0.0, no version-pins.md pin crossed), not excepted.

exceptions.tier: prod-runtime (not loaded by the library entry point)
exceptions.reason: `sprintf-js` (1.0.3 here; the advisory's vulnerable range is <=1.1.3 and the patched range is `<0.0.0`, i.e. NO fixed version exists on npm, so an override/bump is impossible) reaches apps/api production dependencies through exactly one path. Verified with `pnpm why sprintf-js -r`: apps/api -> mammoth 1.13.0 -> argparse 1.0.10 -> sprintf-js 1.0.3, no other consumer in the workspace. GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c is a denial of service through unbounded precision specifiers in a format string passed to sprintf(). Read mammoth's package: `argparse` is required ONLY by `mammoth/bin/mammoth` (the command-line tool, parsing argv for the CLI); a grep of mammoth/lib and the browser bundle for `argparse` finds nothing, so the library entry point that apps/api imports (`require('mammoth')` in resume-text-extraction.service.ts) never loads argparse and therefore never loads sprintf-js. apps/api does not run the mammoth CLI. Even if argparse were loaded, its sprintf calls format its own fixed usage/error templates (`ignored explicit argument %r`, `{ prog }` usage), never a format string derived from an uploaded DOCX or any request data, so the attacker-controlled precision specifier the advisory requires is not reachable. Residual risk accepted: none that reaches a request path. Fix path: re-check when sprintf-js publishes a patched release (then add an override floor), or when mammoth drops its argparse 1.x dependency.
